title: Theo and the Sigil
premise: Rosalind Voss, a nonbinary cartographer who maps realms that shouldn't exist and keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, has survived by being unremarkable—until the crown's witch-hunt forces every gifted person into hiding or the pyre. When Rosalind discovers the king has been bound to a sigil that lets a usurper wear his shape and command his armies, they must ally with Theo, a disgraced royal scribe who once turned them in to save his own skin. As the usurper's armies march on the free cities, Rosalind and Theo fall in love while racing to unbind the king, learning that belonging means choosing each other over safety. In the end, Rosalind breaks the sigil at terrible cost—the king dies free, the usurper's power shatters—but Rosalind survives, no longer invisible, standing with Theo and the guild as the free cities claim their own map.
about_author: Yara Sandoval is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging maps of places that no longer exist before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a coastal town where the fog makes every street feel unmapped.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. We meet the Guild of Impossible Things through its ledgers: bottled storms, doors to elsewhere, a cartographer who draws realms into being. Rosalind keeps the books and stays deliberately dull. Emotional beat: quiet contentment built on careful invisibility, shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Market Bell
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The crown posts a decree: all gifted persons must register or burn. A neighbor is taken within hours. The guild debates scattering; Rosalind argues they can hide in plain sight. Emotional beat: fear arriving like weather, and the first crack in Rosalind's belief that obscurity equals safety.

chapters.title: The Scribe Who Knew My Name
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Royal inspectors arrive led by Theo Aldery, a scribe Rosalind recognizes from academy years—and who once reported a gifted classmate. He looks straight at Rosalind's forged papers and passes them. Emotional beat: dread curdling into suspicion; why would a hunter lie?

chapters.title: What Theo Carries
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo reveals he serves the true king, imprisoned beneath his own crown by a binding sigil; the man on the throne is the usurper wearing him. He needs the guild's impossible things to break it. Emotional beat: guilt and desperation; Theo offers truth as penance for an old betrayal.

chapters.title: A Vote Among Thieves
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The guild votes on whether to help. Old debts, old grudges, and the risk of annihilation surface. It passes by one vote—Rosalind's, cast last. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment; Rosalind realizes they've already stopped being invisible the moment they cared.

chapters.title: The Map That Draws Back
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind attempts to chart the sigil's location by mapping the king's dreamscape—a realm only they can enter. The map begins drawing them in return. Emotional beat: wonder laced with terror; Rosalind's gift is larger and stranger than they admitted.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Register
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The hunt intensifies; a registered friend of Theo's is executed to prove the crown's mercy is a lie. Theo burns his own credentials. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve; Theo chooses rebellion over survival.

chapters.title: Doors to Elsewhere
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The guild opens a forbidden door to move the operation ahead of the armies. On the other side is a version of the capital where the sigil's magic pools visibly. Emotional beat: vertigo and awe; the world is bigger than any ledger.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Smile
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo is summoned before the king-usurper, who suspects nothing but enjoys cruelty. Theo must flatter the thing wearing his sovereign's face. Emotional beat: revulsion masked as loyalty; Theo sees how deep the rot goes.

chapters.title: Between Two Watchfires
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Hiding in the dream-realm's borderlands, Rosalind and Theo keep watch together through one long night. They trade confessions—the classmate he betrayed, the family she erased from her maps. Emotional beat: tenderness kindling; two people deciding to be seen.

chapters.title: The Guild Fractures
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A guild member sells their route to the crown to buy her daughter's freedom. The safehouse falls; half the guild scatters or is captured. Emotional beat: betrayal and heartbreak; Rosalind learns trust is a cost paid in advance, not guaranteed afterward.

chapters.title: Prisoner of Paper
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Captured and interrogated, Rosalind hides the true map inside a forged one, letting the inspectors chase a phantom sigil. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into cunning; Rosalind discovers their invisibility was always a weapon, not just a shelter.

chapters.title: The Rescue Nobody Planned
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo betrays his rank openly, breaking Rosalind out with help from two surviving guild members. He takes a wound meant for them. Emotional beat: fierce gratitude tipping into love; duty finally points the same direction as desire.

chapters.title: Where the King Dreams
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Following the corrected map, they reach the dream-realm's heart: a sleeping king tangled in golden thread, guarded by memories weaponized against intruders. Emotional beat: solemnity; the stakes become human—a tired man, not a symbol.

chapters.title: The First Unbinding Fails
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Their first attempt to cut the sigil rebounds; the binding feeds on identity, and Rosalind nearly loses their own name in the attempt. Emotional beat: despair and humility; some locks cannot be forced, only understood.

chapters.title: Armies at the Free Cities' Gates
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The usurper's host arrives; refugees flood the guild's hidden ways. The remaining members choose to stand rather than flee. Emotional beat: grim solidarity; belonging stops being an idea and becomes a wall people hold together.

chapters.title: The Price Written in Ink
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind understands the sigil: it can only be unbound by someone willing to be fully known—every line of themselves written into the breaking. They begin redrawing their own map, truths included. Emotional beat: terrifying acceptance; love against duty resolves into love as duty freely chosen.

chapters.title: The Throne Room of Threads
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. While Theo distracts the usurper with the forged evidence, Rosalind enters the throne room's dream-layer and writes themselves into the sigil—name, history, love, all of it. The binding shatters; the king wakes; the usurper unravels mid-command. Emotional beat: triumphant sacrifice that refuses to be fatal.

chapters.title: A King, Free and Mortal
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The freed king, aged and diminished, abdicates rather than rule on borrowed legitimacy, charging the free cities to govern themselves. Theo, pardoned and purposeless, wonders where a traitor-scribe belongs now. Emotional beat: bittersweet victory; the war ends but identities must be rebuilt.

chapters.title: Ledgers Opened
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The guild debates whether to remain secret now that gifts are legal. Rosalind proposes opening the ledgers—teaching, mapping, sharing the impossible. Emotional beat: hope institutionalized; invisibility traded for community.

chapters.title: The Map With Two Names
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind finishes the map of the dream-realm and signs it beside Theo's name—an act that scandalizes and delights the guild in equal measure. Emotional beat: joy; love no longer weighed against anything.

chapters.title: Edges of the Known World
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Rosalind and Theo set out to survey the realms beyond the opened doors, leaving copies of every map behind so no one need ever be lost—or hidden—again. Emotional beat: forward-looking peace; belonging carried like a compass rather than clutched like a secret.
